title: Canonical small etale module category and Zariski extension and restriction
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and Zariski site [def-sc-zariski-site]. Define the ring presheaf $\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}$ by $(v:V\to X)\mapsto\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, with restriction by pullback of regular functions, and let $\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}$ also denote its sheaf of rings. Write $\operatorname{Mod}(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}})$ for its category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $j:X_{\mathrm{Zar}}\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$ send an open to its open subscheme. For a proof that $j$ is continuous, the canonical ring map $\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{Zar}}\to j_*\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}$ identifies regular functions on an open with those on its open subscheme. Define $\epsilon_*$ to be restriction along $j$ with restriction of scalars through this map. Given also a proof that $\epsilon_*$ is a right adjoint, define $\epsilon^*$ as the canonical ringed-site tensor pullback $\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\epsilon^{-1}\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{Zar}}}\epsilon^{-1}(-)$. A Zariski-etale module context consists only of these two proof fields, continuity of $j$ and the right-adjoint property of $\epsilon_*$; its restriction and extension functors are the constructions just specified, with no additional chosen functor or map.
